change_summary: The journal has retracted the caffeine and working memory paper. An institutional investigation found that the data in Figures 2 to 4 were fabricated. Those figures show the paper's primary result, n-back accuracy by dose, so its conclusions can't be relied on. The authors have not responded.
evaluation: The draft cites the paper once, in the Introduction, to justify using a 200 mg dose: it says the paper showed a 12% working memory gain at that dose. The paper has been retracted because the data in Figures 2 to 4, which show the accuracy results, were fabricated. The 12% result therefore cannot support the dose choice. Because the dose is a core design parameter of the experiment, this matters a lot for the draft.
recommendation: Raise this with your co-authors or supervisor, and remove or replace the Brown and Kim citation. The journal retracted the paper because its accuracy figures were fabricated, and your draft uses its 12% result to justify the 200 mg dose.
